senses.title: Connected with university study
senses.definition: relating to education, teaching, and research at a college or university
senses.definitionCN: 与学院或大学的教育、教学和研究相关
senses.example: She has a strong academic background.
senses.exampleCN: 她有很强的学术背景。
senses.why: The word comes from the name of Plato's school, and it still points to the world of formal study.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自柏拉图学园的名字，至今仍指向正规研究的世界。

senses.title: The academic year
senses.definition: the period during which a school or university holds classes
senses.definitionCN: 学校或大学开课的那段时间
senses.example: The academic year begins in September.
senses.exampleCN: 学年从九月开始。
senses.why: The adjective marks the calendar of the scholar's world, divided into terms rather than seasons.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记学者世界的日历，按学期而不是按季节划分。

senses.title: Academic achievement
senses.definition: measured performance in study, as shown by grades or results
senses.definitionCN: 以成绩或结果体现的学习表现
senses.example: The school focuses on academic performance.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校注重学业表现。
senses.why: Performance in the scholar's world is measured by examinations rather than by markets.
senses.whyCN: 学者世界里的表现由考试而不是市场来衡量。

senses.title: Academic freedom
senses.definition: the right of teachers and researchers to pursue ideas without political control
senses.definitionCN: 教师与研究者不受政治控制地探究思想的自由
senses.example: The university defends academic freedom.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学捍卫学术自由。
senses.why: The school of Plato was a protected space for argument, and the word keeps that idea of a sheltered zone.
senses.whyCN: 柏拉图学园是一个受保护的论辩空间，这个词保留着「庇护地带」的观念。

intro.en: Academic comes from the name of Plato's school outside Athens, and it has meant the world of formal study ever since.
intro.cn: academic 出自雅典城外柏拉图学园的名字，此后一直指正规研究的世界。

items.en: Modern English uses academic for universities, journals, freedom, and pure theory, and calls a researcher an academic.
items.cn: 现代英语把 academic 用于大学、期刊、自由与纯理论，也把研究者称为 an academic。

items.en: As research universities grew, academic became the standard adjective for their teaching and scholarship.
items.cn: 随着研究型大学发展，academic 成为描述其教学与学术的标准形容词。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English used academic for the schools of ancient philosophy and for learned persons.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语用 academic 指古代哲学的学派，也指有学问的人。

items.en: Latin academicus meant belonging to the Academy, the school founded by Plato.
items.cn: 拉丁语 academicus 意为「属于学园的」，即柏拉图所创的学校。

items.en: Greek Akadēmeia was the grove near Athens where Plato taught, named after the hero Akademos.
items.cn: 希腊语 Akadēmeia 是雅典附近柏拉图讲学的园林，以英雄阿卡德摩斯命名。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same Academy root; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for study, theory, and bookishness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「学园」词根的词；近义组收表示学术、理论与书斋气的形容词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Athenian grove behind the word and the calendar and places of university life.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用这个词背后的雅典园林，以及大学生活的日历与场所。

normal.en: Academy plus ic: the adjective simply says belonging to the school.
normal.cn: academy 加 ic：这个形容词只是表示「属于学园的」。

normal.en: Plato taught in a grove named after a hero, so every academic idea still stands under those trees.
normal.cn: 柏拉图在台北英雄命名的园林里讲学，所以每个学术观念仍站在那些树下。

normal.en: Academic year is the school's calendar, running from first lecture to last exam.
normal.cn: academic year 是学园的日历，从第一堂课走到最后一场考试。

normal.en: A purely academic question is one that only matters inside the grove.
normal.cn: purely academic 的问题，是只在园林里才有分量的问题。

normal.en: Two academics means two people who live and work inside that grove.
normal.cn: two academics 就是两个在那片园林里生活与工作的人。

abstract.en: Picture a walled garden of books: inside, argument is protected; outside, the city goes on without it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座围起来的书园：里面有受保护的论辩，外面的城市照旧运转。

abstract.en: Every sense marks something inside that wall: years, grades, freedom, disciplines, journals, people.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都标记墙内的某样东西：学年、成绩、自由、学科、期刊、人。

abstract.en: The slight insult in purely academic comes from the wall: what matters here may matter nowhere else.
abstract.cn: purely academic 里那点轻微的不屑来自这堵墙：在这里重要的事，别处可能毫不重要。

examples.en: The academic year begins in September with lectures and exams.
examples.cn: 学年在九月开始，伴有授课与考试。

examples.en: She has published in several academic journals.
examples.cn: 她在几份学术期刊上发表过论文。

examples.en: The objection is purely academic.
examples.cn: 这个反对意见纯属理论问题。

senses.title: A school for a special subject
senses.definition: a school that teaches one field, such as music, art, or a trade
senses.definitionCN: 只教授一个领域（如音乐、美术或某种行业）的学校
senses.example: She studied at a music academy in Vienna.
senses.exampleCN: 她曾在维也纳的一所音乐学院学习。
senses.why: The word began as the name of Plato's school, and it still means a place set apart for one kind of learning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是柏拉图学园的名字，至今仍指为某一种学问单独划出的地方。

senses.title: A learned society
senses.definition: an association of scholars or artists who promote a subject
senses.definitionCN: 由学者或艺术家组成、推动某一学科的团体
senses.example: The academy publishes a journal every quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会每季度出版一期期刊。
senses.why: The school became a body of people rather than a building, and the name moved with them.
senses.whyCN: 学校变成了由人组成的团体而不是一栋建筑，名字也跟着人走。

senses.title: A military academy
senses.definition: a college that trains officers for the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 为武装部队培养军官的学院
senses.example: He trained at a military academy.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一所军事学院受训。
senses.why: Modern states borrowed the word for institutions that drill a single profession.
senses.whyCN: 现代国家借这个词指专门训练一种职业的机构。

intro.en: Academy is the name of Plato's grove outside Athens, and it has been applied to schools and learned bodies ever since.
intro.cn: academy 是雅典城外柏拉图园林的名字，此后一直被用于学校与学术团体。

items.en: Modern English uses academy for music schools, military colleges, science bodies, sports programmes, and film awards.
items.cn: 现代英语用 academy 指音乐学校、军事学院、科学团体、体育项目与电影奖项。

items.en: Seventeenth-century learned societies adopted the name for their meetings and publications.
items.cn: 十七世纪的学会采用这个名字来称呼自己的会议与出版物。

items.en: Renaissance writers revived academy for groups of artists and thinkers, giving the word a second life.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的作者复兴了 academy 一词，用来指艺术家与思想家的团体，使它获得第二次生命。

items.en: Latin Academia named the school of Plato and later any philosophical school.
items.cn: 拉丁语 Academia 指柏拉图的学园，后来泛指任何哲学学派。

items.en: Greek Akadēmeia was the grove near Athens where Plato taught, named after the hero Akademos.
items.cn: 希腊语 Akadēmeia 是雅典附近柏拉图讲学的园林，以英雄阿卡德摩斯命名。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same grove; the near-meaning group collects names for schools and learned bodies.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Athenian grove and the modern places that borrowed its name.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用雅典的园林，以及借用它名字的现代场所。

normal.en: Academy is the grove before it is the school: the name travelled from trees to buildings.
normal.cn: academy 先是园林，然后才是学校：名字从树木走到建筑。

normal.en: A military academy drills one profession, exactly as an art academy drills one craft.
normal.cn: 军事学院训练一种职业，正如艺术学院训练一门手艺。

normal.en: An academy of sciences is the grove without students: only the scholars remain.
normal.cn: 科学院是没有学生的园林：只剩下学者。

normal.en: A football academy shows the word can be borrowed by any trade that trains the young.
normal.cn: 足球青训学院说明，任何培养年轻人的行业都能借这个词。

normal.en: The Academy Awards are a society honouring its own craft, with a stage instead of a grove.

abstract.en: Picture a shaded walk where a master and a few students argue under the trees.
abstract.cn: 想象一条有树荫的步道，一位大师和几个学生在树下辩论。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps one element of that walk: a place apart, one subject, and a group of people.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留那次散步的一个要素：一处独立的地方、一个主题、一群人。

abstract.en: The name spread because every profession wanted a grove of its own.
abstract.cn: 这个名字传播开来，因为每种职业都想要一片自己的园林。

scene: 代表们在门外等了很久，直到里面终于传来一声同意。The government refused to accede to the protesters' demands.
sceneCN: 这里 accede to 指答应诉求（第 1 个义项：同意请求）；句意为政府拒绝答应抗议者的要求。

pos.zh: 同意；应允；就任；加入（条约、组织）

senses.title: To agree to a request
senses.definition: to say yes to what someone has asked for
senses.definitionCN: 对别人提出的请求表示同意
senses.example: The committee acceded to the request for more time.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会同意了延长时限的请求。
senses.why: Latin accedere meant to go to, and agreeing is pictured as moving over to the other side's position.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accedere 意为「走向」，同意被想象成走到对方的立场那边。

senses.title: To take up a throne or office
senses.definition: to formally begin to hold a throne or a high public office
senses.definitionCN: 正式开始掌握王位或高级公职
senses.example: She acceded to the throne at eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 她十八岁继承王位。
senses.why: To accede to a throne is to move up to it, the spatial sense applied to rank.
senses.whyCN: accede to a throne 就是走向那个座位，是空间义用在等级上。

senses.title: To join a treaty
senses.definition: to become a formal party to an international agreement
senses.definitionCN: 成为一项国际协议的正式缔约方
senses.example: The country acceded to the treaty in two thousand four.
senses.exampleCN: 该国于二零零四年加入该条约。
senses.why: A treaty is a room others have entered; acceding is walking in.
senses.whyCN: 条约是别人已经进入的房间；加入就是走进去。

senses.title: To yield under pressure
senses.definition: to give in to demands after resisting for some time
senses.definitionCN: 抵抗一段时间后向要求让步
senses.example: The minister finally acceded to pressure from the unions.
senses.exampleCN: 部长最终屈服于工会的压力。
senses.why: The movement here is reluctant: the door opens only because pushing has continued.
senses.whyCN: 这里的动作带着不情愿：门之所以开，是因为推了很久。

intro.en: Accede is Latin for going to something, and its senses are all a movement toward a request, a throne, or a treaty.
intro.cn: accede 在拉丁语中意为「走向某物」，它的义项都是朝请求、王位或条约移动。

items.en: Modern English accedes to requests, thrones, treaties, and organisations, always with a sense of formal movement.
items.cn: 现代英语 accede 用于请求、王位、条约与组织，始终带着正式移动的意味。

items.en: Diplomatic writing fixed accession as the technical term for joining a treaty or an international body.
items.cn: 外交文书把 accession 固定为加入条约或国际机构的技术术语。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English borrowed the verb from French accéder, at first for coming to office and consenting.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语从法语 accéder 借入这个动词，最初指就任与同意。

items.en: Accedere joined ad, to, with cedere, to go, giving the plain sense of going toward.
items.cn: accedere 把表示「朝向」的 ad 与表示「走」的 cedere 组合起来，字面就是「朝……走去」。

items.en: Cedere, to go or yield, also produced proceed, concede, and recede.
items.cn: cedere「走、让步」还产生了 proceed、concede、recede 等词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and nouns from the same going-toward root; the near-meaning group collects verbs for consenting and yielding.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「走向」词根的形式与名词；近义组收表示同意与让步的动词。

entries.definition: The act of taking office or joining a treaty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就任；加入」。

entries.definition: The act of agreeing or joining, in progress.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，义为「正在同意或加入的」。

entries.definition: The act of assenting; a rare synonym of accession.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同意；应允」，属罕用词。

entries.definition: The right or ability to enter or use something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权；使用权」，词形与 accede 相近。

entries.definition: To share the same opinion or consent to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意」。

entries.definition: To give permission or approval.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意；准许」。

entries.definition: To agree formally to a proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「正式同意」，语气正式。

entries.definition: To give way under pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「屈服；让步」。

entries.definition: To admit or give up something unwillingly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认；勉强让步」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin picture of walking toward a door and the formal situations where accede appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「朝门走去」的拉丁画面，以及 accede 出现的正式场合。

normal.en: Ac plus cede: cede means go, so accede is to go toward what is being asked.
normal.cn: ac 加 cede：cede 意为走，所以 accede 就是朝被请求的方向走去。

normal.en: A closed door and a nod inside: the nod is the agreement, the opening is the movement.
normal.cn: 一扇关着的门，里面有人点头：点头是同意，开门是移动。

normal.en: Accede to the throne is the same step, only the chair is higher.
normal.cn: accede to the throne 是同一步，只是椅子更高。

normal.en: Accede to a treaty is walking into a room where other states already stand.
normal.cn: accede to a treaty 就是走进一个别国已经站在里面的房间。

normal.en: Accession is the noun of that step, used in news about kings and unions.
normal.cn: accession 是这一步的名词，见于关于国王与联盟的新闻。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor with one door at the end: consent is the walk, not the words.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长走廊，尽头有一扇门：同意是那段行走，而不是那些话。

abstract.en: Every sense is that walk: toward a request, a throne, a treaty, a union, or another person's argument.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是那段行走：走向请求、王位、条约、联盟，或别人的论证。

abstract.en: The word is formal because the corridor is public, and the step is recorded.
abstract.cn: 这个词之所以正式，是因为走廊是公共的，那一步会被记录。

examples.en: The government refused to accede to the protesters' demands.
examples.cn: 政府拒绝答应抗议者的要求。

examples.en: She acceded to the throne at eighteen.
examples.cn: 她十八岁继承王位。

examples.en: The country acceded to the treaty in two thousand four.
examples.cn: 该国于二零零四年加入该条约。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses agree to a request, take a throne, join a treaty, and yield under pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项分别是应允请求、即位、加入条约，以及在压力下让步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person walking toward a closed door and being admitted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人朝关着的门走去，并被允许进入。

branches.en: THE CONSENT: a request is granted.
branches.cn: 应允线：请求被答应。

branches.en: THE THRONE: a ruler takes the seat of power.
branches.cn: 继位线：君主坐上权位。

branches.en: THE TREATY: a state becomes a party to an agreement.
branches.cn: 缔约线：国家成为协定的一方。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE: agreement is given because one is pushed.
branches.cn: 让步线：因为被推着，才表示同意。

branches.en: THE JOINING: consenting and becoming a party are one motion toward an arrangement.
branches.cn: 加入线：应允与成为一方，都是朝同一项安排靠近。

intro.en: Accede is built from a Latin prefix of direction and a verb of going.
intro.cn: accede 由表示方向的拉丁前缀与表示「走」的动词构成。

definition_zh: 加速；促进；提前
definition_en: to make something move faster or happen sooner
core_image: 一辆车踩下油门，速度表的指针向右甩
scene: 绿灯一亮，司机踩下踏板，车子立刻冲了出去。The new software accelerates the processing of large files.
sceneCN: 这里 accelerates 指加快处理速度（第 2 个义项：使过程加快）；句意为新软件加快了大文件的处理。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ion 构成，义为「加速；加速度」
由动词加 -or 构成，义为「加速器；油门」
由动词加 -ive 构成，义为「加速的」
由动词加 -ant 构成，义为「助燃剂；促进剂」
由 accelerator 与 meter 合成，义为「加速度计」

senses.title: To make a vehicle go faster
senses.definition: to press the control that increases the speed of a car or other vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 踩下使汽车等交通工具速度提高的操纵装置
senses.example: The driver accelerated out of the junction.
senses.exampleCN: 司机加速驶出路口。
senses.why: Latin celer meant swift, and the verb simply makes something more swift than it was.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 celer 意为「迅速」，这个动词就是让某物比原来更迅速。

senses.title: To make a process happen faster
senses.definition: to reduce the time a process takes without changing its steps
senses.definitionCN: 不改变步骤而缩短一个过程所需的时间
senses.example: New software accelerates the processing of large files.
senses.exampleCN: 新软件加快了大文件的处理。
senses.why: The image of a speedometer carries over: the same work is done, but the pointer sits higher.
senses.whyCN: 速度表的意象延续下来：同样的工作被完成，只是指针停在更高的位置。

senses.title: To hasten economic growth
senses.definition: to increase the rate at which an economy or business expands
senses.definitionCN: 提高经济或企业扩张的速度
senses.example: The tax cut accelerated growth in the first quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 减税加快了第一季度的增长。
senses.why: Growth has a rate, and accelerating it means pushing that rate upward.
senses.whyCN: 增长有一个速率，加速就是把那个速率往上推。

senses.title: To speed up particles
senses.definition: to increase the velocity of subatomic particles in an apparatus
senses.definitionCN: 在装置中提高亚原子粒子的速度
senses.example: The machine accelerates protons to high energy.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器把质子加速到高能。
senses.why: Physics uses the word at its most literal: a charged particle is given more speed.
senses.whyCN: 物理学用的是最字面的义项：给带电粒子更大的速度。

intro.en: Accelerate comes from the Latin word for swift, and it has always meant adding speed to something.
intro.cn: accelerate 出自拉丁语中表示「迅速」的词，历来都指给某物增加速度。

items.en: Modern English accelerates vehicles, processes, growth, particles, schedules, learning, and repayment.
items.cn: 现代英语加速车辆、流程、增长、粒子、日程、学习与还款。

items.en: Physics gave the word its technical noun acceleration, the rate at which velocity changes.
items.cn: 物理学给了这个词技术名词 acceleration，即速度变化的比率。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English borrowed the verb from Latin, first in learned writing about motion.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语从拉丁语借入这个动词，最初出现在关于运动的学术写作中。

items.en: Accelerare joined ad, toward, with celerare, to make swift, from celer, swift.
items.cn: accelerare 把表示「朝向」的 ad 与 celerare「使迅速」组合起来，后者出自 celer「迅速的」。

items.en: Celer meant swift and survives in the English noun celerity, meaning speed.
items.cn: celer 意为「迅速的」，仍活在英语名词 celerity（迅速）中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and instruments from the same swift root; the near-meaning group collects verbs for speeding up.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「迅速」词根的形式与器具；近义组收表示加快的动词。

entries.definition: The rate at which speed increases.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加速；加速度」。

entries.definition: A pedal or machine that increases speed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「油门；加速器」。

entries.definition: An instrument that measures acceleration.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加速度计」。

entries.definition: Swiftness of movement or action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「迅速；敏捷」，与 accelerate 同出 celer。

entries.definition: A substance that makes a fire spread faster.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「助燃剂」。

entries.definition: To make something happen sooner.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「催促；使提早发生」。

entries.definition: To make or become faster.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加快」。

entries.definition: To make a process happen more quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加速办理；促进」，语气正式。

entries.definition: To move forward or bring something to an earlier time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「前进；提前」。

entries.definition: To move or cause to move faster.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「加快速度」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the speedometer picture and the different things the word can push faster.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用速度表的画面，以及这个词能推快的各种东西。

normal.en: Ac plus celer: celer means swift, so accelerate is to add swiftness.
normal.cn: ac 加 celer：celer 意为迅速，所以 accelerate 就是增加迅速。

normal.en: A foot on the pedal and a needle swinging right: that needle is the whole word.
normal.cn: 脚踩踏板、指针向右甩：那根指针就是这个词的全部。

normal.en: Physics gives the same picture a number: acceleration is how fast the needle swings.
normal.cn: 物理学给同一画面一个数字：加速度就是指针甩得多快。

normal.en: An accelerator is the pedal, an accelerometer is the gauge, acceleration is the reading.
normal.cn: accelerator 是踏板，accelerometer 是仪表，acceleration 是读数。

normal.en: The word can push bad trends too: inflation accelerates as easily as growth.
normal.cn: 这个词也能推快坏趋势：通胀和增长一样容易加速。

abstract.en: Picture a needle on a dial: the target may be a car, a company, a particle, or a deadline, but the needle is always speed.
abstract.cn: 想象表盘上的一根指针：目标可以是汽车、公司、粒子或截止日期，但指针永远是速度。

abstract.en: Every sense measures the same thing, the rate, and never the destination.
abstract.cn: 每个义项衡量的都是同一样东西——速率，而从不衡量终点。

abstract.en: That is why the word is neutral: it can accelerate a cure or a disaster.
abstract.cn: 这正是这个词保持中立的原因：它能加速治愈，也能加速灾难。

examples.en: The new software accelerates the processing of large files.
examples.cn: 新软件加快了大文件的处理。

examples.en: The tax cut accelerated growth in the first quarter.
examples.cn: 减税加快了第一季度的增长。

examples.en: They accelerated the launch by two months.
examples.cn: 他们把上线时间提前了两个月。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses make speed rise: a vehicle, a process, economic growth, and a particle in a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都让速度上升：车辆、过程、经济增长，以及机器里的粒子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speedometer needle swinging to the right.
core.cn: 核心意象：速度表的指针向右甩。

branches.en: THE VEHICLE: the pedal adds speed.
branches.cn: 车辆线：踏板加上速度。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: a change that used to be slow runs faster.
branches.cn: 过程线：原本缓慢的变化跑得更快。

branches.en: THE ECONOMY: growth is treated as a moving body.
branches.cn: 经济线：增长被当作一个运动中的物体。

branches.en: THE PARTICLE: a machine drives matter to higher energy.
branches.cn: 粒子线：机器把物质推向更高的能量。

branches.en: THE SPEED: physical and abstract motion share one measure.
branches.cn: 速度线：具体与抽象的运动共用同一尺度。

definition_en: the way a group pronounces a language, stress on a syllable, or a mark over a letter
core_image: 说话时某个音节被抬高，像话音里的一块凸起
scene: 同一个词，从她嘴里出来时总有一个音节被抬得特别高。He spoke English with a strong French accent.
sceneCN: 这里 accent 指口音（第 1 个义项：口音）；句意为他说英语带着浓重的法国口音。

pos.zh: 口音；重音；强调；变音符号

senses.title: A way of pronouncing a language
senses.definition: the characteristic pronunciation of a group, region, or nation
senses.definitionCN: 某个群体、地区或民族特有的发音方式
senses.example: He spoke English with a strong French accent.
senses.exampleCN: 他说英语带着浓重的法国口音。
senses.why: Latin accentus meant a song added to speech, and pronunciation is the melody a speaker adds to words.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accentus 意为「加在言语上的歌声」，口音就是说话者给词句加上的旋律。

senses.title: Stress on a syllable
senses.definition: the extra force given to one syllable of a word
senses.definitionCN: 一个词中某一音节获得的额外力度
senses.example: The accent falls on the second syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 重音落在第二个音节上。
senses.why: The same musical idea applies inside a word: one beat is struck harder than its neighbours.
senses.whyCN: 同样的音乐观念用在词内部：一拍比旁边的拍子敲得更重。

senses.title: Emphasis on an idea
senses.definition: special importance given to a point in speech, writing, or design
senses.definitionCN: 在言语、文字或设计中赋予某一点特别的重要性
senses.example: The report puts the accent on prevention.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把重点放在预防上。
senses.why: To accent an idea is to strike its beat harder so the listener hears it first.
senses.whyCN: 强调一个观念，就是把它的拍子敲得更重，让听者先听见。

senses.title: A written mark over a letter
senses.definition: a small mark above a letter that shows stress or a different sound
senses.definitionCN: 字母上方表示重音或不同读音的小符号
senses.example: The word carries an acute accent on the e.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词的 e 上带有一个尖音符。
senses.why: The mark is the musical stress made visible: a small sign where the voice should rise.
senses.whyCN: 这个符号是音乐重音的可见形式：在声音该抬起的地方做一个小记号。

intro.en: Accent is Latin for a song added to speech, a translation of a Greek term for musical pitch in language.
intro.cn: accent 在拉丁语中意为「加在言语上的歌声」，是对希腊语中「语言音高」术语的翻译。

items.en: Modern English uses accent for regional speech, syllable stress, emphasis, written marks, music, and local character.
items.cn: 现代英语用 accent 指地方口音、音节重音、强调、书面符号、音乐重音与地方特色。

items.en: Sixteenth-century teachers used the word for the stress marks printed in school texts.
items.cn: 十六世纪的教师用这个词指课本上印的重音符号。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word through French and used it for the stress of the voice.
items.cn: 中古英语经法语借入这个词，用于嗓音的轻重。

items.en: Latin accentus joined ad, to, with cantus, song, meaning a song added to a spoken word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 accentus 把表示「附加」的 ad 与 cantus「歌」组合起来，意为「加在词上的歌」。

items.en: Cantus meant song or singing and also gives English chant and canticle.

normal.en: Ac plus cent: think of a hundred small marks where the voice rises.
normal.cn: ac 加 cent：想象一百个小记号，标出声音抬起的地方。

normal.en: Latin accentus is a song added to a word: the tune you add is your accent.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 accentus 是加在词上的歌：你加上的那支曲子就是你的口音。

normal.en: A stress mark is the song written down: a small sign over the vowel.
normal.cn: 重音符号是把那支歌写下来：元音上方的一个小记号。

normal.en: Put the accent on a point means make its beat louder than the rest.
normal.cn: put the accent on 某一点，就是让它的拍子比其余更响。

normal.en: Accentuate is the verb of the same idea: make the feature sing.
normal.cn: accentuate 是同一观念的动词：让那个特征唱起来。

abstract.en: Picture a plain sentence with one word sung louder: that louder word is the accent.
abstract.cn: 想象一句平直的话里有一个词唱得更响：那个更响的词就是重音。

abstract.en: Move the loud word to a whole people, and it becomes an accent; write it over a letter, and it becomes a mark.
abstract.cn: 把更响的词移到一整个民族，它就成了口音；把它写在字母上，它就成了符号。

abstract.en: Every sense is emphasis placed somewhere by someone.

definition_zh: 接受；同意；承认；相信；接纳
definition_en: to receive something willingly, agree to it, or admit it as true
core_image: 一只手伸出去，把递来的东西接住
scene: 她把那封录取信拿在手里，看了很久才放进包里。He accepted the job offer without hesitation.
sceneCN: 这里 accepted 指接受工作邀请（第 1 个义项：接受给予之物）；句意为他毫不犹豫地接受了这份工作。

pos.zh: 接受；同意；承认；相信；接纳

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ance 构成，义为「接受；认可；接纳」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可接受的；合意的」

由过去分词转作形容词，义为「公认的；被接受的」

senses.title: To receive something offered
senses.definition: to take willingly something that another person offers or gives
senses.definitionCN: 愿意拿走别人提供或给予的东西
senses.example: He accepted the job offer without hesitation.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫不犹豫地接受了这份工作。
senses.why: Latin accipere meant to take to oneself, and the open hand is the oldest picture of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accipere 意为「拿到自己这里」，张开的手是这个词最古老的画面。

senses.title: To agree to a plan or terms
senses.definition: to say yes to an arrangement that has been put to you
senses.definitionCN: 对摆在你面前的安排表示同意
senses.example: She accepted the terms of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 她接受了合同条款。
senses.why: Agreeing is receiving a proposal into your own plans, as if taking a package indoors.
senses.whyCN: 同意就是把一个提议收进自己的计划，像把包裹拿进屋里。

senses.title: To admit a fact
senses.definition: to admit that something is true even if it is unwelcome
senses.definitionCN: 承认某事为真，即使它并不受欢迎
senses.example: He accepted that the mistake was his.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认那个错误是他的。
senses.why: The hand here takes an unwelcome parcel, because the fact will not go away if refused.
senses.whyCN: 这里的手接过一个不受欢迎的包裹，因为事实即使被拒绝也不会消失。

senses.title: To believe something is true
senses.definition: to regard a statement or claim as true
senses.definitionCN: 把某种说法或主张视为真实
senses.example: Most readers accepted the story as fact.
senses.exampleCN: 多数读者把这个故事当作事实接受。
senses.why: Belief is receiving an idea and letting it stay, rather than turning it away at the door.
senses.whyCN: 相信就是接收一个观念并让它留下，而不是把它挡在门外。

senses.title: To admit someone into a group
senses.definition: to allow a person to join a school, team, or society
senses.definitionCN: 允许某人加入学校、团队或团体
senses.example: The college accepted her for the autumn term.
senses.exampleCN: 学院录取她秋季入学。
senses.why: An institution opens its door, and the person is taken inside as a member.
senses.whyCN: 机构打开门，人被作为成员接进里面。

senses.title: To come to terms with a situation
senses.definition: to stop fighting an unpleasant situation and live with it
senses.definitionCN: 不再与不快的处境抗争，而是与之共处
senses.example: She slowly accepted life in the new city.
senses.exampleCN: 她慢慢接受了在这座新城市的生活。
senses.why: Acceptance here is a long receiving, repeated until the hand stops resisting.
senses.whyCN: 这里的接受是一个漫长的接收过程，反复进行直到手不再抗拒。

intro.en: Accept is Latin for taking something to oneself, and all its senses are versions of an open hand.
intro.cn: accept 在拉丁语中意为「把某物拿到自己这里」，它的所有义项都是「张开的手」的不同版本。

items.en: Modern English accepts offers, terms, facts, beliefs, students, situations, cards, and blame.
items.cn: 现代英语接受提议、条件、事实、信念、学生、处境、银行卡与责任。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English borrowed the verb through French and used it for receiving gifts and opinions.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语经法语借入这个动词，用于接受礼物与意见。

items.en: Middle English used accepten in legal writing for taking an obligation or a payment.
items.cn: 中古英语在法律文书中用 accepten 表示承担义务或收受款项。

items.en: Acceptare was a frequentative form of accipere, meaning to receive repeatedly or habitually.
items.cn: acceptare 是 accipere 的反复形式，意为「反复或习惯性地接收」。

items.en: Accipere joined ad, to, with capere, to take, giving the plain sense of taking something toward oneself.
items.cn: accipere 把表示「朝向」的 ad 与表示「拿」的 capere 组合起来，字面就是「把东西拿到自己这里」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and nouns from the same take-to-oneself root; the near-meaning group collects verbs for receiving and agreeing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「拿到自己这里」词根的形式与名词；近义组收表示接收与同意的动词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the open-hand picture and the objects the verb most often takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「张开的手」的画面，以及这个动词最常接的宾语。

normal.en: Ac plus cept: cept means take, so accept is to take what is handed to you.
normal.cn: ac 加 cept：cept 意为拿，所以 accept 就是拿走递给你的东西。

normal.en: An open hand is the whole word: refusing is a closed fist.
normal.cn: 张开的手就是这个词的全部：拒绝是握紧的拳头。

normal.en: Accept responsibility is an invisible parcel you agree to hold.
normal.cn: accept responsibility 是一个你同意抱住的隐形包裹。

normal.en: A college accepts a student the way a house accepts a guest: the door opens.
normal.cn: 学院录取学生，就像房子接纳客人：门开了。

normal.en: Acceptable, acceptance, accepted: the family all keep the same open hand.
normal.cn: acceptable、acceptance、accepted：这一家子都保留着同一只张开的手。

abstract.en: Picture a hand at a doorway: what comes in is welcome, what stays outside is refused.
abstract.cn: 想象门口的一只手：进来的受欢迎，留在外面的被拒绝。

abstract.en: Every sense is that doorway: gifts, plans, facts, beliefs, people, situations, payments, blame.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是那道门：礼物、计划、事实、信念、人、处境、付款、责任。

abstract.en: The word is not passive: the hand must choose to stay open.
abstract.cn: 这个词不是被动的：手必须选择保持张开。

examples.en: The minister accepted responsibility for the delay.

senses.title: The act of receiving something
senses.definition: the act of taking something that has been offered or sent
senses.definitionCN: 拿走已被提供或寄来的东西的行为
senses.example: The acceptance of the gift surprised the donor.
senses.exampleCN: 收下这份礼物让捐赠者很意外。
senses.why: The noun names the moment the open hand closes around what it has been given.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的正是张开的手合拢、握住所受之物的那一刻。

senses.title: Agreement to terms
senses.definition: the act of agreeing to a contract, offer, or set of conditions
senses.definitionCN: 对合同、提议或一组条件表示同意的行为
senses.example: The deal awaits written acceptance.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易尚待书面同意。
senses.why: A contract is a parcel taken indoors, and acceptance is the moment it is inside.
senses.whyCN: 合同是一个被拿进屋里的包裹，acceptance 就是它进门的时刻。

senses.title: Official approval
senses.definition: recognition or approval given by an authority or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 由权威或行业给予的承认或批准
senses.example: The drug received acceptance from the regulator.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药物获得了监管机构的认可。
senses.why: The hand here belongs to an institution, and what it receives is a standard.
senses.whyCN: 这里的手属于一个机构，它接收的是一套标准。

senses.title: Being welcomed into a group
senses.definition: the state of being admitted and treated as a member by others
senses.definitionCN: 被允许加入并被他人当作成员对待的状态
senses.example: Her acceptance into the programme surprised no one.
senses.exampleCN: 她被项目录取，谁也不感到意外。
senses.why: A door opens and stays open: acceptance is not one greeting but a place among people.
senses.whyCN: 门打开并保持开着：接纳不是一次问候，而是在人群中的一个位置。

senses.title: An offer of admission
senses.definition: a formal letter or notice saying that a place has been granted
senses.definitionCN: 正式说明已获得某个名额的信件或通知
senses.example: The acceptance arrived on a Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 录取通知在周五寄到。
senses.why: The abstract act becomes paper: the open door is written down and posted.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的行为变成了纸：那扇敞开的门被写下来并寄出。

intro.en: Acceptance is the noun of the open hand: it names the moment something is taken in, approved, or admitted.

items.en: Modern English speaks of acceptance letters, acceptance rates, social acceptance, and the acceptance of loss.

items.en: Banking gave the noun a technical sense: a formal promise to honour a bill of exchange.

items.en: Middle English used acceptance for the receiving of a gift, an office, or a legal tender.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the door-and-hand picture and the documents and phrases the noun now names.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「门与手」的画面，以及这个名词现在命名的文件与说法。

normal.en: Accept plus ance: the verb becomes a thing, the moment the hand closes.
normal.cn: accept 加 ance：动词变成一个东西，即手合拢的那一刻。

normal.en: An acceptance letter is the open door written on paper and posted.
normal.cn: acceptance letter 是那扇敞开的门被写在纸上并寄出。

normal.en: Acceptance rate measures how many hands closed out of how many reached out.
normal.cn: acceptance rate 衡量伸出的手中有多少只合拢了。

normal.en: Social acceptance means a whole society has opened its door to a practice.
normal.cn: social acceptance 意为整个社会对某种做法打开了门。

normal.en: In finance, acceptance is a signature that receives a bill and promises to pay.
normal.cn: 在金融里，acceptance 是一枚接收票据并承诺付款的签名。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway with a hand on each side: one offers, the other chooses to receive.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门，两边各有一只手：一只递出，另一只选择接收。

abstract.en: Every sense is a completed doorway: a gift taken, a term agreed, a standard approved, a member admitted, a loss borne.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是一道完成的门：礼物被收下、条款被同意、标准被认可、成员被接纳、失去被承受。

abstract.en: The noun always marks a threshold that has been crossed, not a feeling that has been had.
abstract.cn: 这个名词始终标记一道已经被跨过的门槛，而不是一种已经被拥有的感受。

examples.en: Her acceptance into the programme surprised no one.
examples.cn: 她被项目录取，谁也不感到意外。

examples.en: The deal awaits written acceptance.
examples.cn: 这笔交易尚待书面同意。

examples.en: The practice slowly gained social acceptance.
examples.cn: 这种做法慢慢获得了社会认可。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses cover taking an offered thing, agreeing to terms, official approval, being received by a group, and an offer of a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项覆盖收下递来的东西、同意条件、官方认可、被团体接纳，以及录取通知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door held open while a hand receives what comes through.
core.cn: 核心意象：门被扶着敞开，一只手接收穿过来的东西。

branches.en: THE TAKING: the act of receiving what is offered.
branches.cn: 收受线：接下递来之物的行为。

branches.en: THE TERMS: agreement to a contract or condition.
branches.cn: 同意线：对条款或条件的答应。

branches.en: THE APPROVAL: an authority says yes.
branches.cn: 认可线：权威方面表示同意。

branches.en: THE GROUP: a person is received into a circle.
branches.cn: 归入线：人被一个圈子收下。

branches.en: THE PLACE: a school offers a seat.
branches.cn: 录取线：学校给出一个位置。

intro.cn: acceptance 是建立在「接收」动词上的拉丁行为名词，带状态后缀。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is accipere, acceptare, and acceptatio.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 accipere、acceptare 与 acceptatio。

definition_zh: 通道；进入；使用权；访问；接近
definition_en: the way or right to enter a place, use something, or reach a person
core_image: 一条通往门口的路，被门禁挡着或放行
scene: 保安看了一眼证件，把侧门打开，让他们进去。Students have access to the online library from home.
sceneCN: 这里 access 指使用权（第 3 个义项：使用权）；句意为学生在家也能使用在线图书馆。

pos.zh: 通道；进入权；使用权；访问

derivatives.zh: 由词根加 -ible 构成，义为「可到达的；可使用的；易理解的」
由 accessible 加 -ity 构成，义为「可及性；无障碍性」

senses.title: A way in
senses.definition: a route or opening by which a place can be entered
senses.definitionCN: 可以进入某处的路线或开口
senses.example: The only access to the beach is a narrow path.
senses.exampleCN: 去海滩的唯一通道是一条窄路。
senses.why: Latin accessus meant an approach, and the word still begins with a physical way in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessus 意为「接近」，这个词至今仍从一条具体的进入之路开始。

senses.title: The right to enter
senses.definition: permission to enter a building, area, or event
senses.definitionCN: 进入建筑、区域或活动的许可
senses.example: Journalists were denied access to the site.
senses.exampleCN: 记者被拒绝进入现场。
senses.why: A door can be open and still guarded, so access becomes a permission as well as a path.
senses.whyCN: 门可以开着却仍有人看守，于是 access 除了路径，也成了许可。

senses.title: The right to use something
senses.definition: the opportunity or right to use a service, system, or resource
senses.definitionCN: 使用某项服务、系统或资源的机会或权利
senses.example: Students have access to the online library.
senses.exampleCN: 学生可以使用在线图书馆。
senses.why: Use needs an entry point too, even when nothing physical is opened.
senses.whyCN: 使用也需要一个入口，即使并没有打开任何实物。

senses.title: The ability to reach a person
senses.definition: the opportunity to speak with someone important or powerful
senses.definitionCN: 与重要或有权力的人交谈的机会
senses.example: Few reporters have access to the minister.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有记者能接触到部长。
senses.why: A person can be treated as a guarded room, and access is the chance to enter it.
senses.whyCN: 一个人可以被当作一间有人看守的房间，而 access 就是进入它的机会。

senses.title: An access road
senses.definition: a road built to lead vehicles to a main route or a site
senses.definitionCN: 为把车辆引向主干道或某场地而修建的道路
senses.example: The new access road shortens the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 新的通道公路缩短了行程。
senses.why: This is the first sense made of asphalt: a way in for wheels.
senses.whyCN: 这是第一个义项铺上了沥青：为车轮准备的进入之路。

intro.en: Access is Latin for an approach, and it has widened from a physical way in to a right, a connection, and a permission.
intro.cn: access 在拉丁语中意为「接近」，它从一条具体的进入之路，扩展为权利、连接与许可。

items.en: Modern English speaks of access roads, internet access, access codes, and access to ministers.
items.cn: 现代英语说通道公路、网络接入、访问码与接触部长的机会。

items.en: Computing gave the word a new object: users access files, and systems control access.
items.cn: 计算机给这个词一个新的宾语：用户访问文件，系统控制访问。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English used access for the act of approaching a person or a place.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语用 access 指接近某人或某地的行为。

items.en: Latin accessus was a noun of action from accedere, meaning a coming near or an approach.
items.cn: 拉丁语 accessus 是 accedere 的行为名词，意为「靠近、接近」。

items.en: Accedere joined ad, to, with cedere, to go, giving the picture of walking toward a door.
items.cn: accedere 把表示「朝向」的 ad 与表示「走」的 cedere 组合起来，画面就是朝门走去。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same approach root; the near-meaning group collects nouns for entry and availability.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「接近」词根的词；近义组收表示进入与可获得性的名词。

entries.definition: Able to be reached, used, or understood.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可到达的；可使用的；易懂的」。

entries.definition: The quality of being easy to reach or use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可及性；无障碍性」。

entries.definition: The act of taking office or joining a treaty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就任；加入」，与 access 同出 accedere。

entries.definition: Reached or opened, as data or a place.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，义为「被访问的；被进入的」。

entries.definition: In the act of reaching or using.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，义为「正在访问的」。

entries.definition: The act of coming in, or a way in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入；入口」。

entries.definition: A door or gate through which one enters.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「入口；大门」。

entries.definition: Permission to enter a place or organisation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准许进入；入场」。

entries.definition: The act of coming near, or a way of dealing with something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「接近；方法」。

entries.definition: The state of being ready for use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可获得性；可用性」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the door-and-road picture and the modern systems that now use the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「门与路」的画面，以及现在使用这个词的现代系统。

normal.en: Ac plus cess: cess means go, so access is a going toward the door.
normal.cn: ac 加 cess：cess 意为走，所以 access 就是朝门走去。

normal.en: A guarded door can be open and still refuse: that is why access also means permission.
normal.cn: 有人看守的门可以开着却仍拒绝：这正是 access 也表示许可的原因。

normal.en: Access road, access code, access control: the word builds modern compounds as easily as old ones.
normal.cn: access road、access code、access control：这个词造现代复合词和造旧词一样容易。

normal.en: The verb access is what the computer does when it opens a file.
normal.cn: 动词 access 就是计算机打开文件时做的事。

normal.en: Accessible and accessibility are the adjective and noun of the open door.
normal.cn: accessible 与 accessibility 是那扇敞开的门的形容词与名词。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor with one door at the end and a guard beside it: path, permission, and person all meet there.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，尽头有一扇门，旁边有守卫：路径、许可与人都在那里相遇。

abstract.en: Every sense is that meeting point, whether the door leads to a beach, a library, a minister, a network, or a building.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是那个相遇点，无论门后是海滩、图书馆、部长、网络还是一栋楼。

abstract.en: The word always asks two questions at once: is there a way, and are you allowed?
abstract.cn: 这个词总是同时问两个问题：有没有路，你被允许吗？

examples.cn: 学生在家也能使用在线图书馆。

examples.en: Journalists were denied access to the site.
examples.cn: 记者被拒绝进入现场。

examples.en: The building uses card-based access control.
examples.cn: 这栋楼使用刷卡门禁。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses cover a way in, the right to enter, the right to use, the ability to approach a person, and a road that carries traffic.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项覆盖进入的路、进入的权利、使用的权利、接近某人的机会，以及承载车流的道路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corridor leading to a guarded door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条通向有人看守之门的走廊。

branches.en: THE WAY IN: a passage that leads inside.
branches.cn: 通道线：通向内部的通路。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: permission to enter.
branches.cn: 权利线：获准进入。

branches.en: THE USE: permission to make use of something.
branches.cn: 使用线：获准使用某物。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the chance to approach someone.
branches.cn: 接近线：有机会靠近某人。

branches.en: THE ROAD: a route built for traffic.
branches.cn: 道路线：为车流修建的路线。

senses.title: Able to be reached
senses.definition: possible to reach, especially after some effort
senses.definitionCN: 可以到达，尤指需要一番努力之后
senses.example: The village is accessible only by boat.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子只能乘船到达。
senses.why: Latin accessibilis meant approachable, and the oldest sense is simply a place one can walk to.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessibilis 意为「可接近的」，最古老的义项就是人能走到的地方。

senses.title: Available to those who need it
senses.definition: open or available to a particular group of people
senses.definitionCN: 向特定人群开放或可供其获得
senses.example: The service is accessible to all residents.
senses.exampleCN: 这项服务对所有居民开放。
senses.why: The door is not only reachable but unlocked for a named group.
senses.whyCN: 门不仅可以走到，而且为特定人群打开了锁。

senses.title: Easy to use or understand
senses.definition: simple enough for ordinary people to use or follow
senses.definitionCN: 简单到普通人也能使用或跟上
senses.example: The guide is accessible to beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这本指南初学者也看得懂。
senses.why: A text or tool with a wide door lets more people in, so the word moves from space to comprehension.
senses.whyCN: 门开得宽的文字或工具能让更多人进来，于是这个词从空间移到理解。

senses.title: Designed without barriers
senses.definition: built so that people with disabilities can enter and use it
senses.definitionCN: 为让残障人士能够进入和使用而建造
senses.example: The museum is fully wheelchair accessible.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆完全可供轮椅通行。
senses.why: Modern design made the old metaphor a duty: no step may block a body.
senses.whyCN: 现代设计把古老的比喻变成义务：没有一级台阶可以挡住一种身体。

senses.title: Easy to talk to
senses.definition: said of a person who is friendly and easy to approach
senses.definitionCN: 指一个人友好、容易接近
senses.example: The director is accessible to junior staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这位主管对下级员工很平易近人。
senses.why: A person, like a building, can have a closed or open door.
senses.whyCN: 一个人像一栋建筑，可以有紧闭的门，也可以有敞开的门。

intro.en: Accessible is the Latin adjective of approach, and its senses widen the doorway from a path to a format.
intro.cn: accessible 是拉丁语中表示「可接近」的形容词，它的义项把门口从一条路扩展到一种格式。

items.en: Modern English calls places, services, texts, people, and formats accessible, and law requires many of them to be so.
items.cn: 现代英语称场所、服务、文本、人与格式为 accessible，法律还要求其中许多必须如此。

items.en: Accessibility legislation made the adjective a standard that buildings and websites must meet.
items.cn: 无障碍立法使这个形容词成为建筑与网站必须达到的标准。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English used accessible for places and persons that could be approached.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语用 accessible 指可以接近的场所与人。

items.en: Accessibilis was formed from accessus, an approach, and meant that could be gone to.
items.cn: accessibilis 由 accessus「接近」构成，意为「可以走到的」。

items.en: The verb accedere, to go toward, supplies the root picture of walking to a door.
items.cn: 动词 accedere「朝……走去」提供了走向一扇门的词根画面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same approach root; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for reachable, available, and approachable.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「接近」词根的词；近义组收表示可达、可用与平易的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being accessible.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可及性；无障碍性」。

entries.definition: In an easy-to-reach way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「可接近地；易懂地」。

entries.definition: Impossible or very hard to reach.

entries.definition: The act of taking office or joining.

entries.definition: Able to be arrived at.

entries.definition: Ready for use or obtainable.

entries.definition: Clear enough to be understood.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可理解的」。

entries.definition: Friendly and easy to talk to.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「平易近人的」。

entries.definition: Not closed, or free for anyone to use.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「开着的；开放的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the no-threshold door and the many kinds of door the adjective now describes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「没有门槛的门」，以及这个形容词现在描写的各种门。

normal.en: Access plus ible: a door that can be passed through.
normal.cn: access 加 ible：一扇可以穿过去的门。

normal.en: Think of a shop with no step at the entrance: everyone can walk in without help.
normal.cn: 想象一家入口没有台阶的商店：谁都能不用别人帮忙就走进去。

normal.en: A website with screen-reader support is a ramp for the ears.
normal.cn: 支持屏幕阅读器的网站，是给耳朵的坡道。

normal.en: An accessible writer opens the door of a difficult subject.
normal.cn: accessible 的作者会打开难懂主题的那扇门。

normal.en: Inaccessible is the same door with the key turned.
normal.cn: inaccessible 是同一扇门，只是钥匙转了一圈。

abstract.en: Picture a building whose only entrance is a low, wide opening with no step at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋建筑，唯一的入口是一个低而宽、完全没有台阶的开口。

abstract.en: Every sense removes one kind of step: distance, price, jargon, disability, rank, transport, format.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都移除一种台阶：距离、价格、术语、残障、等级、交通、格式。

abstract.en: The word always asks who is still standing outside.

core.cn: 核心意象：一道既没有台阶也没有锁的门口。

branches.en: THE REACH: a place one can get to.
branches.cn: 到达线：能够去到的地方。

branches.en: THE OBTAINING: something one can get hold of.
branches.cn: 取得线：能够拿到的东西。

branches.en: THE UNDERSTANDING: a text or idea within reach of the reader.
branches.cn: 理解线：读者够得着的文本或想法。

branches.en: THE DESIGN: a building that does not exclude bodies.
branches.cn: 设计线：不把某些身体排除在外的建筑。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a figure one can talk to without fear.
branches.cn: 人际线：可以不怕地与之交谈的人物。

definition_en: the act of taking up office, joining a treaty, or adding something to a collection
core_image: 一本登记册上写下新名字，把新来者正式记入
scene: 博物馆把新到的画作登记入册，编号写在标签上。The library announced the accession of a rare manuscript.
sceneCN: 这里 accession 指新藏品入藏（第 5 个义项：新增藏品）；句意为图书馆宣布入藏一份珍本手稿。

senses.title: Taking up a throne or office
senses.definition: the act of formally beginning to rule or hold a high office
senses.definitionCN: 正式开始统治或担任高级公职的行为
senses.example: Her accession to the throne was widely reported.
senses.exampleCN: 她继承王位的消息被广泛报道。
senses.why: Latin accedere means to go toward, and taking a throne is moving up to the seat.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accedere 意为「走向」，登上王位就是走向那个座位。

senses.title: Joining a treaty
senses.definition: the formal act by which a state becomes party to an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 一国成为某协议缔约方的正式行为
senses.example: The accession to the treaty took effect in May.
senses.exampleCN: 加入条约于五月生效。
senses.why: A treaty is a room already occupied, and accession is the recorded entry.
senses.whyCN: 条约是一个已经有人的房间，accession 是被记录下来的入场。

senses.title: Joining a union or organisation
senses.definition: the process by which a country joins a political or economic union
senses.definitionCN: 一国加入政治或经济联盟的过程
senses.example: The accession talks lasted four years.
senses.exampleCN: 入盟谈判持续了四年。
senses.why: The doorway is now a negotiating table, and the word names the whole approach.
senses.whyCN: 门口现在是一张谈判桌，这个词命名的是整段接近的过程。

senses.title: Adding to a collection
senses.definition: the act of adding an item to a library, museum, or archive
senses.definitionCN: 把一件物品加入图书馆、博物馆或档案馆的行为
senses.example: The accession of the archive took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这批档案的入藏花了两年。
senses.why: A collection has a door too: new items are received and written into the register.
senses.whyCN: 收藏也有一道门：新物品被接收，并被写进登记册。

senses.title: An item added to a collection
senses.definition: a single object or document newly added to a collection
senses.definitionCN: 新加入收藏的单件物品或文件
senses.example: The library announced the accession of a rare manuscript.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆宣布入藏一份珍本手稿。
senses.why: The act and the object share one noun: what comes in is itself an accession.
senses.whyCN: 行为与物品共用一个名词：进来的东西本身就是一件 accession。

intro.en: Accession is the noun of going toward something, and it now covers thrones, treaties, unions, and museum registers.
intro.cn: accession 是「走向某物」的名词，现在覆盖王位、条约、联盟与博物馆登记册。

items.en: Modern English uses accession for royal succession, treaty entry, union membership, and archive intake.
items.cn: 现代英语用 accession 指王位继承、条约加入、联盟成员资格与档案入藏。

items.en: European integration made accession the standard word for a state joining the union.
items.cn: 欧洲一体化使 accession 成为一国加入联盟的标准说法。

items.en: Museums and libraries adopted accession for the register of newly received objects.
items.cn: 博物馆与图书馆采用 accession 指新收物品的登记。

items.en: Latin accessio meant an approach or an addition, formed from the verb accedere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 accessio 意为「接近、增添」，由动词 accedere 构成。

items.en: Accedere joined ad, to, with cedere, to go, giving the picture of walking up to a place.
items.cn: accedere 把表示「朝向」的 ad 与表示「走」的 cedere 组合起来，画面就是走向某处。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same going-toward root; the near-meaning group collects nouns for taking office and adding.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「走向」词根的词；近义组收表示就任与增添的名词。

normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「登记册与门口」的画面，把王位、条约与博物馆连起来。

normal.en: Accession is accede turned into a noun: the step through the door, written down.
normal.cn: accession 是 accede 的名词形式：穿过门的那一步，被写了下来。

normal.en: A king's accession is a step up; a treaty's accession is a step in; a museum accession is a step onto a shelf.
normal.cn: 国王的 accession 是向上一步；条约的 accession 是向里一步；博物馆的 accession 是上架一步。

normal.en: Accession number is the receipt for that step.

normal.en: Accession talks are the long corridor before the door.

normal.en: The old sense, formal consent, is still the same movement of the mind.

abstract.en: Picture a ledger open on a desk: every entry is a person or an object that has crossed a threshold.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上摊开的登记册：每一条记录都是一个跨过门槛的人或物。

abstract.en: Every sense is an entry in that ledger: a reign begun, a treaty signed, a union joined, a manuscript received.

abstract.en: The word always marks an official beginning, never a private feeling.

definition_zh: 配件；附件；服饰配件；附属物；从犯；附属的；副的
definition_en: an extra item that improves the look or usefulness of something else, or a person who helps another in a crime
core_image: 一件挂在本体旁边的小物件：不改变主体，只让它更完整
scene: 舞台后台的化妆台上摆着几串项链和一条腰带，演员正在挑今晚的搭配。She chose a silver necklace as the last accessory for her stage costume.
sceneCN: 这里 accessory 指服饰配件（第 2 个义项：首饰、包、腰带等装饰性物件）；句意为她挑了一条银项链作为舞台服装的最后一件配饰。

pos.zh: 名词：配件；附件；服饰配件；从犯
形容词：附属的；附加的；副的

senses.title: An extra piece that completes a thing
senses.definition: a small item added to something larger and more important in order to make it more useful or complete
senses.definitionCN: 附加在更大、更主要的事物上的小物件，用来让它更有用或更完整
senses.example: Every printer in the office comes with a set of accessories.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室里的每台打印机都配有一套附件。
senses.why: Latin accessorius named something that stands near another thing, so an accessory is literally the item that comes alongside the main one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessorius 指「站在另一物旁边的东西」，因此 accessory 字面上就是陪在主体旁边的那件物品。

senses.title: A fashion item worn for style
senses.definition: a bag, belt, scarf, hat or piece of jewellery that finishes an outfit
senses.definitionCN: 包、腰带、围巾、帽子或首饰，用来完成整体穿着
senses.example: A plain dress can be lifted by a bright accessory at the waist.
senses.exampleCN: 一条素色连衣裙，靠腰间的亮色配饰就能出彩。
senses.why: Clothing is the main body and decoration is what comes beside it, so the old idea of nearness turned into the language of style.
senses.whyCN: 衣服是主体，装饰是陪在旁边的东西，于是「在旁边」这一古老含义变成了时尚领域的说法。

senses.title: An attachment for equipment
senses.definition: a device or part that is attached to a machine to give it an extra function
senses.definitionCN: 加装在机器上、为其增加一项功能的装置或部件
senses.example: The drill kit includes a sanding accessory for wood.
senses.exampleCN: 这套电钻工具包含一个用于木材的打磨附件。
senses.why: The accessory does not replace the machine; it sits beside it and adds a new use, exactly as accessorius described.
senses.whyCN: 附件并不取代机器，而是在旁边为它增加一种用途，这正是 accessorius 所描述的关系。

senses.title: A secondary part of a system
senses.definition: a part that supports a main system without being central to it
senses.definitionCN: 支撑主系统、但本身并不处于核心位置的部件
senses.example: The pump is an accessory unit that feeds the main engine.
senses.exampleCN: 这台泵是为主发动机供料的附属机组。
senses.why: Engineers borrowed the word to rank parts: the main unit carries the load, and everything near it is accessory.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用了这个词来给部件分级：主机组承担负荷，陪在旁边的都是附属件。

senses.title: A helper in a crime, after the fact
senses.definition: a person who helps an offender escape or hide the evidence after the crime has been committed
senses.definitionCN: 在犯罪已经发生之后帮助罪犯逃脱或隐藏证据的人
senses.example: He was charged as an accessory after the fact for hiding the stolen car.
senses.exampleCN: 他因藏匿被盗车辆而被认定为事后从犯。
senses.why: Law kept the adverb of nearness: someone who stands close to the crime but does not commit it is an accessory.
senses.whyCN: 法律保留了「在旁边」这一含义：站在罪行旁边、但并未亲手实施的人，就是从犯。

intro.en: Accessory began as a Latin word for what stands near a main thing, and it now names both a fashion item and a helper in a crime.
intro.cn: accessory 最初是拉丁语中表示「站在主体旁边之物」的词，如今既指时尚配饰，也指罪案中的从犯。

items.en: In current English an accessory is usually a bag, belt or piece of jewellery that finishes an outfit, a sense that grew with department stores.
items.cn: 在现代英语里，accessory 通常指包、腰带或首饰等完成整体造型的物件，这一义项随百货商店的兴起而流行。

items.en: Legal writers fixed the phrases accessory before the fact and accessory after the fact for people who help a crime from outside.
items.cn: 十九世纪的法律作者固定了 accessory before the fact 与 accessory after the fact 两个短语，指从旁协助犯罪的人。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the noun covered any added item, while the adjective meant additional or subordinate.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个名词泛指任何附加之物，形容词则意为「附加的」或「从属的」。

items.en: Accessorius was formed from accessor, one who comes near, and described a thing attached to another thing.
items.cn: accessorius 由 accessor「走近的人」构成，用来描述附着于另一物的东西。

items.en: The verb accedere, to come near, joins ad- toward with cedere go, and it is the same root as access.
items.cn: 动词 accedere 意为「走近」，由 ad-「朝向」与 cedere「走」组成，与 access 同根。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same approach root; the near-meaning group gathers words for added pieces and for helpers in a crime.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「走近」词根的词；近义组收表示附加物与罪案帮手的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picture of a small thing standing beside a larger one.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想用「小物件站在大物件旁边」这一画面。

normal.en: Access plus ory: the thing that comes near the main object.
normal.cn: access 加 ory：靠近主体放置的那件东西。

normal.en: A phone case is an accessory: the phone works without it, but looks better with it.
normal.cn: 手机壳就是 accessory：没有它手机也能用，但有了它更好看。

normal.en: On a stage the costume is the main act and the necklace is an accessory.
normal.cn: 舞台上戏服是主角，项链只是 accessory。

normal.en: In law the accessory stands beside the principal offender, close but secondary.
normal.cn: 法律上，从犯站在主犯旁边，关系很近，但地位次要。

normal.en: Accessorize is the verb: to add the finishing pieces.
normal.cn: accessorize 是动词，意为「添上点睛的配饰」。

abstract.en: Picture a main body with a small satellite that never leaves its side.
abstract.cn: 想象一个主体，旁边永远跟着一颗小小的卫星。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps the idea of nearness: a near item, a near part, a near helper.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留「在旁边」这一核心：旁边的物件、旁边的部件、旁边的帮手。

abstract.en: The legal sense turns nearness into guilt, because helping from the side still counts.
abstract.cn: 法律义项把「在旁边」变成了罪责，因为从旁协助同样算数。

examples.en: She bought a silk scarf as an accessory for her winter coat.
examples.cn: 她买了一条丝巾，作为冬季大衣的配饰。

examples.en: The camera comes with a full set of accessories, including a spare battery.
examples.cn: 这台相机配有一整套附件，其中包括一块备用电池。

examples.en: He was charged as an accessory to the robbery.
examples.cn: 他被指控为这起抢劫案的从犯。

root: 拉丁语 accedere「走近」→ accessor「靠近的人」→ accessorius「附属的」→ 英语 accessory。核心是「在旁边」：在衣服旁边的配饰、在机器旁边的附件、在主体旁边的次要部件、在罪行旁边的从犯。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses name an extra part, an item of dress, a device add-on, a subordinate piece, and a person who aids a crime.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项分别指附加部件、服饰配件、设备附加件、附属构件，以及协助犯罪的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small item standing beside a larger one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件小物件站在更大的物件旁边。

branches.en: THE EXTRA: something added to the main thing.
branches.cn: 附件线：加在主物之上的东西。

branches.en: THE DRESS: what completes an outfit.
branches.cn: 服饰线：让一身穿戴完整的东西。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: an add-on for a machine.
branches.cn: 设备线：机器的附加件。

branches.en: THE SUBORDINATE: a part that serves another part.
branches.cn: 附属线：为另一部分服务的部件。

branches.en: THE COMPLICE: a person who helps without doing the act.
branches.cn: 从犯线：不出手却协助的人。

intro.en: Accessory is built from a Latin verb of approach plus a suffix of relation, and it has a regular noun, verb and adjective family.
intro.cn: accessory 由拉丁语「走近」动词加关系后缀构成，并拥有规则的名词、动词与形容词家族。

definition_zh: 事故；意外事件；偶然；偶性；（保险）意外事故
definition_en: an unexpected event, especially one that causes injury or damage, or a chance occurrence rather than a planned one
core_image: 一件从手里滑落的东西：它本不在计划里，落地时却改变了局面
scene: 雨夜的十字路口停着两辆变形的车，警示灯一亮一暗。No one was hurt in the accident, but the road stayed closed for an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 accident 指交通事故（第 1 个义项：车辆碰撞一类的事故）；句意为事故中没有人受伤，但道路封闭了一小时。

pos.zh: 名词：事故；意外事件；偶然；偶性

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「意外的；偶然的」
由 accidental 加 -ly 构成，义为「偶然地；意外地」
由本词加 -prone 构成，义为「易出事故的」

senses.title: A crash on the road
senses.definition: an unexpected collision or crash that damages vehicles and injures people
senses.definitionCN: 车辆相撞或失控等意外，造成车辆损坏与人员受伤
senses.example: The accident at the junction sent two drivers to hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 路口发生的交通事故把两名司机送进了医院。
senses.why: The oldest sense of something falling upon a person turned into the modern scene of metal meeting metal.
senses.whyCN: 「某件事落到人身上」这一最古老的含义，演变成今天金属相撞的画面。

senses.title: An injury at work
senses.definition: an unplanned event at a workplace that injures a worker or damages equipment
senses.definitionCN: 工作场所中造成工人受伤或设备损坏的意外事件
senses.example: The factory reported a serious accident on the assembly line.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂报告了装配线上一起严重事故。
senses.why: Once work moved into large plants, the chance event that falls on a body became a matter of safety rules and reports.
senses.whyCN: 当劳动进入大型工厂，「落到身体上的偶然事件」就成了安全规程与事故报告的问题。

senses.title: An unlucky chance event
senses.definition: an unfortunate event that happens without plan and brings loss or pain
senses.definitionCN: 没有计划却发生、带来损失或痛苦的不幸事件
senses.example: Losing the manuscript was a cruel accident of timing.
senses.exampleCN: 手稿丢失是时机造成的残酷意外。
senses.why: The core of the word is not the damage but the absence of intention: nothing was aimed at, yet something arrived.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心不是损害，而是「没有意图」：没有人瞄准，事情却发生了。

senses.title: Something done without plan
senses.definition: an action or result that comes about by chance rather than by design
senses.definitionCN: 因偶然而非因设计产生的行为或结果
senses.example: Meeting her at the station was a happy accident.
senses.exampleCN: 在车站遇见她是一次幸运的偶然。
senses.why: Here the word loses its dark colour: chance can be kind, and an accident can be a gift rather than a loss.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词失去了阴沉的色彩：偶然也可以是善意的，accident 也能是礼物而非损失。

intro.en: Accident comes from a Latin verb meaning to fall upon. The word began as a description of chance and only later settled into the modern sense of a crash or injury.
intro.cn: accident 来自一个意为「落到……上」的拉丁动词。它最初描述偶然，后来才固定为现代「事故、伤害」的含义。

items.en: Today an accident is mainly a crash or an injury, and the phrase accident and emergency names the hospital unit that treats them.
items.cn: 今天 accident 主要指撞车或受伤，短语 accident and emergency 则指处理这类情况的医院急诊科。

items.en: Railways and factories made sudden injuries common enough for accident insurance and accident-prone to enter everyday speech.
items.cn: 铁路与工厂让突发伤害变得常见，accident insurance 与 accident-prone 由此进入日常语言。

items.en: English writers used accident for anything that happened by chance, and the phrase by accident fixed the idea of doing something unintentionally.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语作者用 accident 指任何偶然发生的事，短语 by accident 则固定了「并非有意」的含义。

items.en: Accidens, the present participle of accidere, was used by translators of Aristotle for a property that merely happens to a thing.
items.cn: accidens 是 accidere 的现在分词，亚里士多德的译者用它指「恰好附属于某物」的属性。

items.en: Accidere joins ad- toward and cadere to fall, so the root picture is something falling onto a person or a place.
items.cn: accidere 由 ad-「朝向」与 cadere「落下」组成，词根画面就是某物落到人或地点之上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same fall or the same event pattern; the near-meaning group gathers words for crashes and for misfortune.
note.cn: 形近组收同出「落下」词根或同一事件模式的词；近义组收表示撞车与不幸的词。

entries.definition: The part of grammar dealing with word endings and forms.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「词形变化学」，与 accident 拼写极近但含义无关。

entries.definition: An event, often a minor or unpleasant one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件；小事故」，与 accident 形近而重「事件」。

entries.definition: Happening by chance, not on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「意外的；偶然的」。

entries.definition: In a way that is not planned.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「偶然地；意外地」。

entries.definition: Likely to have accidents often.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「易出事故的」。

entries.definition: A small accident or unlucky event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小事故；不幸的意外」，语气比 accident 轻。

entries.definition: A violent collision of vehicles or objects.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「撞车；碰撞」，强调撞击的猛烈。

entries.definition: The act of two moving objects hitting each other.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「相撞」，是较中性的技术说法。

entries.definition: Bad luck or an unlucky event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不幸；厄运」，侧重命运而非撞击。

entries.definition: The happening of events without any known cause or plan.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「偶然；机会」，是 accident 的抽象对应词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picture of something falling out of a hand and landing where nobody planned.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想用「东西从手里滑落、落在没人预料的地方」这一画面。

normal.en: Accident looks like ad plus cadere, something falling toward you without warning.
normal.cn: accident 可拆成 ad 加 cadere，像某物毫无预警地朝你落下。

normal.en: A car accident is metal falling onto metal.
normal.cn: 车祸就是金属砸到金属。

normal.en: By accident means the hand was open when it should have been closed.
normal.cn: by accident 意味着手该握紧时却松开了。

normal.en: Accident insurance pays for the fall nobody planned.
normal.cn: 意外保险赔付的就是那场没人计划过的跌落。

normal.en: An accident of the land is a bump that the map did not intend to draw.
normal.cn: 地形的偶然起伏，是地图本没打算画出的那个小包。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that slips from a ledge and lands on a path where a walker happens to stand.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头从岩架滑落，恰好砸在散步者站着的路上。

abstract.en: Every sense removes the human plan: no aim, no schedule, no design.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都抽掉了人的计划：没有瞄准、没有日程、没有设计。

abstract.en: Philosophy keeps the purest form: a property that merely falls onto a thing.
abstract.cn: 哲学保留了最纯粹的形式：一种仅仅「落到」某物上的属性。

examples.en: He was injured in a car accident on the way to work.
examples.cn: 他在上班途中的车祸里受了伤。

examples.en: I found the old letter by accident while cleaning the attic.
examples.cn: 我在清理阁楼时偶然发现了那封旧信。

examples.en: The company offers accident insurance to all its drivers.
examples.cn: 公司为所有司机提供意外伤害保险。

root: 拉丁语 accidere「落到……上」→ accidens「偶发之事」→ 英语 accident。核心是「没有计划的降临」：落到人身上的车祸与工伤、落到生活里的偶然、落到事物上的非本质属性、落到地表上的小起伏。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses cover a road crash, a workplace injury, an unlucky event, and anything that happens by chance.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项覆盖交通事故、工伤、不幸的意外，以及任何偶然发生的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something falls onto a person or place without warning.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物毫无预警地落到人或地点之上。

branches.en: THE ROAD: vehicles meet with damage.
branches.cn: 交通线：车辆相遇并造成损伤。

branches.en: THE WORKPLACE: a machine injures a worker.
branches.cn: 工伤线：机器伤到工人。

branches.en: THE MISFORTUNE: an event that hurts and was not wanted.
branches.cn: 意外线：造成伤害且并非所愿的事件。

branches.en: THE CHANCE: whatever happens without a plan.
branches.cn: 偶然线：没有计划而发生的任何事。

branches.en: THE SCENE: road and workplace are two places where the same noun is used first.
branches.cn: 现场线：道路与工地是这个词最常出现的两个现场。

intro.cn: accident 是拉丁语「朝向」与「落下」的复合词，其词族按规则的形容词、副词与后缀模式构成。

latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 cadere、accidere 与 accidens。

definition_zh: 赞誉；喝彩；公开称赞；拥立；好评
definition_en: to praise someone or something publicly and with enthusiasm, or the loud approval that such praise produces
core_image: 一群人仰起头，朝台上的人大声喊出肯定
scene: 首映结束，灯光亮起，观众站成一排鼓掌，影评人也在低声议论。The director was acclaimed for a film that had taken ten years to finish.
sceneCN: 这里 acclaim 指公开称赞（第 1 个义项：公开赞扬某人或其作品）；句意为这位导演因一部耗时十年的影片受到赞誉。

pos.zh: 动词：公开称赞；欢呼拥立

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「广受赞誉的」
由拉丁语 acclamatio 借入，义为「欢呼；喝彩；鼓掌通过」
由 acclamation 加 -ory 构成，义为「表示欢呼的」

senses.title: To praise publicly
senses.definition: to praise a person, work or action openly and with strong approval
senses.definitionCN: 公开而强烈地赞许某人、某作品或某行为
senses.example: Reviewers acclaimed the novel as a masterpiece.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者称赞这部小说是杰作。
senses.why: Latin acclamare meant to shout toward someone, so praise begins as a loud voice aimed at the person on stage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acclamare 意为「朝某人喊叫」，所以称赞最初是朝台上之人发出的响亮声音。

senses.title: To declare someone something
senses.definition: to declare a person to be a king, leader or winner by general agreement
senses.definitionCN: 以众人一致的方式宣布某人为国王、领袖或获胜者
senses.example: The crowd acclaimed him captain after the final whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响后，人群拥立他为队长。
senses.why: A shout can do more than praise: when enough voices agree, the shout turns into an official declaration.
senses.whyCN: 喊声不止是称赞：当足够多的声音一致时，喊声就变成了正式的宣布。

senses.title: Loud applause from an audience
senses.definition: the noise of cheers and clapping that a crowd makes to show approval
senses.definitionCN: 人群为表示赞许而发出的欢呼与掌声
senses.example: The singer stepped out to the acclaim of the whole hall.
senses.exampleCN: 歌手在全场掌声中走上舞台。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical sound: approval measured in decibels rather than in printed words.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了物理的声音：赞许以分贝来衡量，而不是以文字来衡量。

senses.title: Praise from critics
senses.definition: approval expressed by reviewers and experts, especially for a film, book or play
senses.definitionCN: 影评人、书评人等专业人士表达的赞许，尤指对电影、书或戏剧
senses.example: Her first collection earned critical acclaim but sold few copies.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部诗集获得了评论界的好评，但销量很少。
senses.why: Modern culture separated the loud crowd from the quiet reviewer, and acclaim now covers both kinds of approval.
senses.whyCN: 现代文化把喧闹的人群与安静的评论者分开，而 acclaim 现在同时覆盖这两种赞许。

intro.en: Acclaim is a Latin shout turned into praise. It first named the noise of welcome and later grew into the language of reviews and reputations.
intro.cn: acclaim 是一个由「喊叫」变成「称赞」的拉丁词。它最初指欢迎的声响，后来发展成评论与声誉的语言。

items.en: Film festivals and review pages made critical acclaim a standard phrase, and an acclaimed actor is one whose work has been praised.
items.cn: 电影节与评论版面使 critical acclaim 成为固定说法，而 acclaimed 演员指的是作品受到称赞的演员。

items.en: The phrase by popular acclaim recorded appointments made by a crowd rather than by a formal ballot.
items.cn: 短语 by popular acclaim 记录了靠人群而非正式投票作出的任命。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the verb meant both to shout in welcome and to declare someone a ruler.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个动词既表示欢呼迎接，也表示宣布某人为统治者。

items.en: Acclamare joined ad- toward with clamare to shout, and described a cry directed at a person.
items.cn: acclamare 由 ad-「朝向」与 clamare「喊叫」组成，描述朝某人发出的呼喊。

items.en: Clamare, to cry out, also gave English exclaim, claim and clamour, all built on the same loud voice.
items.cn: clamare 意为「大声喊」，还产生了英语的 exclaim、claim 与 clamour，它们都建立在同一个「响亮的声音」上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the shout root; the near-meaning group gathers words for praise and applause.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「喊叫」词根的词；近义组收表示称赞与鼓掌的词。

entries.definition: Loud and enthusiastic approval.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「欢呼；喝彩；鼓掌通过」。

entries.definition: Expressing cheers or approval.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「表示欢呼的」。

entries.definition: Widely praised, especially by critics.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「广受赞誉的」。

entries.definition: To cry out suddenly because of strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「呼喊；惊叫」，与 acclaim 同出 clamare。

entries.definition: A loud and confused noise of many voices.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喧嚷；吵闹」，同出 clamare。

entries.definition: To express approval or admiration.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「称赞；赞扬」，是最中性的对应词。

entries.definition: To clap the hands to show approval.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「鼓掌」，侧面对现场的动作。

entries.definition: To praise formally or officially.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「表扬；嘉许」，语气偏正式。

entries.definition: To greet or describe as great.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欢呼致意；称颂」，带公开宣告色彩。

entries.definition: To shout in encouragement or joy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欢呼；喝彩」，强调声音而非评价。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picture of a crowd shouting approval at someone standing above them.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想用「人群朝站在高处的人大声喊出赞许」这一画面。

normal.en: Acclaim sounds like a claim shouted out: the crowd claims that this person is great.
normal.cn: acclaim 听起来像被喊出来的 claim：人群宣称这个人了不起。

normal.en: Picture the exclamation mark above a theatre: the louder the praise, the higher the mark.
normal.cn: 想象剧院上方有一个感叹号：赞许喊得越响，符号就立得越高。

normal.en: Critical acclaim is praise written down; popular acclaim is praise shouted out.
normal.cn: critical acclaim 是写下来的赞许，popular acclaim 是喊出来的赞许。

normal.en: An acclaimed film is one that the crowd has already shouted about.
normal.cn: acclaimed 影片指的是人群已经为之呼喊过的影片。

normal.en: By popular acclaim means the crowd itself did the voting with its voice.
normal.cn: by popular acclaim 意为人群用声音完成了投票。

abstract.en: Picture a single voice starting in the back row and the whole hall joining in.
abstract.cn: 想象后排的一个声音先起，随后整个大厅跟着一起喊。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps a public sound: praise is never silent.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留一种公开的声音：赞许从来不是沉默的。

abstract.en: The noun turns the sound into a reputation that travels beyond the hall.
abstract.cn: 名词把声音变成一种能传出大厅之外的声誉。

examples.en: The film won critical acclaim at the festival.
examples.cn: 这部影片在电影节上获得评论界的好评。

examples.en: Critics acclaimed her performance as the best of the year.
examples.cn: 评论者称赞她的演出是当年最佳。

examples.en: The crowd acclaimed the returning champion with cheers.
examples.cn: 人群以欢呼迎接归来的冠军。

definition_en: to provide enough space or lodging for someone, or to adjust so that different needs can fit together
core_image: 把房间的尺寸调到刚好装下所有人，谁也不必挤在门外
scene: 会议室里椅子一圈圈加到最后几乎贴着墙，组织者还在数人头。The hall was built to accommodate six hundred people, and every seat was taken.
sceneCN: 这里 accommodate 指容纳（第 1 个义项：在空间或数量上容纳）；句意为大厅按容纳六百人设计，而每个座位都坐满了。

pos.zh: 动词：容纳；提供住处；适应；迁就；顾及；调解

collocations.zh: 接待客人；为客人提供住处

senses.title: To hold a number of people
senses.definition: to provide enough room for a number of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 为一群人或一批物品提供足够的空间
senses.example: The stadium can accommodate forty thousand spectators.
senses.exampleCN: 这座体育场能容纳四万名观众。
senses.why: Latin accommodare meant to make a thing fit a measure, so the first sense is simply a room that fits its crowd.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accommodare 意为「使某物合于尺度」，因此第一个义项就是「装得下人群的空间」。

senses.title: To give someone lodging
senses.definition: to provide a room or place to stay for a guest, traveller or group
senses.definitionCN: 为客人、旅客或团体提供房间或住处
senses.example: The family accommodated three students during the conference.
senses.exampleCN: 会议期间这家人接待了三名学生住宿。
senses.why: A room is the most concrete kind of space that fits a person, so lodging grew naturally from the idea of making room.
senses.whyCN: 房间是最具体的一种「装得下人」的空间，因此「提供住处」自然地从「腾出空间」发展而来。

senses.title: To adjust to a new condition
senses.definition: to change oneself or a system so that it works in new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 改变自身或系统，使其在新条件下正常运作
senses.example: The eye accommodates to darkness within a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛在几分钟内就能适应黑暗。
senses.why: The fitting is no longer spatial: an organism or a system reshapes itself until it matches the new measure.
senses.whyCN: 这种「合于尺度」不再是空间上的：生物或系统重新调整自身，直到与新尺度相合。

senses.title: To oblige someone
senses.definition: to do what someone wants in order to help or please them
senses.definitionCN: 为了帮助或取悦某人而按他的意愿行事
senses.example: The manager accommodated her request for a later shift.
senses.exampleCN: 经理通融了她晚班的要求。
senses.why: When the measure is another person, fitting means bending your own schedule to their shape.
senses.whyCN: 当尺度变成了另一个人，合于尺度就意味着把自己的安排弯向对方的形状。

senses.title: To take different needs into account
senses.definition: to include the needs or views of several people or groups in a plan
senses.definitionCN: 在计划中纳入若干人或群体的需要与看法
senses.example: The design accommodates both wheelchair users and cyclists.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计同时顾及轮椅使用者与骑行者的需要。
senses.why: One room must now fit several shapes at once, so the verb shifts from making space to balancing claims.
senses.whyCN: 同一个空间要同时装下几种形状，于是这个动词从「腾出空间」转为「平衡各种诉求」。

senses.title: To reconcile two claims
senses.definition: to bring two ideas or accounts into agreement without destroying either
senses.definitionCN: 使两种观点或说法达成一致，而不破坏其中任何一方
senses.example: The report accommodates the findings of both research teams.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告调和了两个研究团队的结论。
senses.why: Mediation is fitting at a higher level: two accounts are adjusted until they occupy the same frame.
senses.whyCN: 调解是更高层次的「合于尺度」：两种说法被调整到能同处一个框架。

intro.en: Accommodate comes from a Latin verb meaning to fit a thing to a measure. From fitting a room to fitting a person, it widened into adjustment and reconciliation.
intro.cn: accommodate 来自一个意为「使某物合于尺度」的拉丁动词。从「装下空间」到「配合他人」，它的含义扩展为适应与调和。

items.en: Hotels, halls and stadiums advertise how many guests they can accommodate, and the verb has become a plain statement of capacity.
items.cn: 旅馆、礼堂与体育场都宣传自己能容纳多少客人，这个动词已成为对容量的平实陈述。

items.en: Optics borrowed the word for the eye, and accommodation named the lens adjusting to the distance of an object.
items.cn: 光学借用了这个词来描述眼睛，accommodation 指晶状体对物体距离所作的调节。

items.en: The phrase accommodate oneself to a situation fixed the modern sense of adjusting to circumstances.
items.cn: 短语 accommodate oneself to a situation 固定了现代「适应环境」的含义。

items.en: Accommodare joined ad- toward with commodare to make suitable, and meant to fit one thing to another.
items.cn: accommodare 由 ad-「朝向」与 commodare「使适合」组成，意为「使一物合于另一物」。

items.en: Commodus meant fitting or convenient, built from com- together and modus measure, so the root picture is a thing cut to the right size.
items.cn: commodus 意为「合适的；方便的」，由 com-「共同」与 modus「尺度」构成，词根画面就是按合适的尺寸裁好的一件东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the measure root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for holding, housing and adjusting.
note.cn: 形近组收同出「尺度」词根的词；近义组收表示容纳、住宿与调整的动词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picture of measuring a room until every guest fits inside.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想用「把房间量了又量，直到每位客人都装得下」这一画面。

normal.en: Accommodate contains the word mode: to find the right mode for each person.
normal.cn: accommodate 里藏着 mode：为每个人找到合适的模式。

normal.en: Picture a hotel clerk moving beds until every guest has a room.
normal.cn: 想象旅馆前台不断挪动床位，直到每位客人都有一间房。

normal.en: A hall that can accommodate six hundred people has been measured for six hundred chairs.
normal.cn: 能容纳六百人的大厅，是按六百把椅子量过的。

normal.en: To accommodate a request is to cut your plan to the shape of the asker.
normal.cn: 满足一个请求，就是把自己的计划裁成请求者的形状。

normal.en: The eye accommodates by changing its lens, not its mind.
normal.cn: 眼睛靠改变晶状体来调节，而不是改变想法。

abstract.en: Picture a carpenter shaving a door until it closes without a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象木匠把门刨了又刨，直到它关上时没有缝隙。

abstract.en: Every sense fits one thing to another: a crowd to a hall, a guest to a bed, a plan to a need.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在让一物合于另一物：人群合于大厅、客人合于床、计划合于需要。

abstract.en: The legal and diplomatic sense fits two claims into one frame without breaking either.
abstract.cn: 法律与外交的义项，是把两种主张装进同一个框架，而不弄坏任何一方。

examples.en: The new hall can accommodate up to eight hundred guests.
examples.cn: 新礼堂最多可容纳八百位客人。

examples.en: The hotel accommodated us in a larger room when our flight was delayed.
examples.cn: 航班延误时，旅馆把我们安排进了一间更大的房间。

examples.en: Good managers accommodate different working styles.
examples.cn: 优秀的管理者会顾及不同的工作方式。

definition_en: a place to live or stay, or the act of adjusting something so that it fits a person or a need
core_image: 把原本放不下的东西挪一挪，腾出刚够容身的空间
scene: 开学第一周，新生在校园附近找落脚的地方，房东把一间小屋腾出来给她。The university guarantees accommodation to every first-year student who applies in time.
sceneCN: 这里 accommodation 指学校提供的住处（第 1 个义项：住处）；句意为凡按时申请的一年级学生都能得到住宿保障。
